response: {"title":"Dependency-fanout targeting","intervention":"Before finalizing, run exactly one available check under a timeout of 10% of the task deadline, selecting the check that covers the changed module with the largest downstream dependency fanout and breaks ties by shorter expected runtime.","claim":"Compared with no appended instruction, dependency-fanout targeting will increase hidden-test pass_rate without increasing deadline misses, median wall_time, or turns by more than 5%.","mechanism":"Failures in high-fanout modules can invalidate many downstream paths, so testing the most propagated risk first maximizes expected caught failures per bounded verification run.","assumptions":["The repository structure reveals approximate module dependency fanout","At least one check covers a changed high-fanout module","One bounded check can finish within 10% of the deadline"],"risks":["Fanout is an imperfect proxy for defect probability","A low-fanout module may contain the actual severe bug","The chosen check may not exercise the changed behavior","Startup overhead may consume the timeout"],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomly assign matched multi-module Python tasks to treatment or no-instruction control with identical model, seed, tools, and deadline; score hidden tests, completion time, and interaction count.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"Treatment has higher pass_rate, no greater deadline-miss rate, and median wall_time and turns no more than 5% above control."},"single_shot_ordinal":4}
